# Data

**These files are synthetic.** They are generated by `generate_synthetic_data.py`
and contain no real company data.

## Why synthetic

The original coursework used the **Supply Chain Logistics Problem Dataset**
(Kalganova, T. & Dzalbs, I., 2019, Brunel University London,
[doi.org/10.17633/rd.brunel.7558679](https://doi.org/10.17633/rd.brunel.7558679)) —
outbound logistics data from a global microchip producer. That dataset is not
redistributed here.

Instead, the generator reproduces the three structural features of the original
that drive the model's behaviour, so results are comparable in kind:

| Feature | Original | Synthetic |
|---|---|---|
| Warehouses × destinations | 19 × 7 | 19 × 7 |
| Model size | 159 variables | 159 variables |
| Total demand | 29,513,315 | 29,513,315 |
| Total capacity | 5,791 | 5,791 |
| Capacity as % of demand | 0.02% | 0.02% |
| Demand at largest destination | 96.9% | 96.9% |
| Lanes with observed (not imputed) cost | 10 of 143 (7.0%) | 9 of 133 (6.8%) |
| Transportation cost reduction | 5.6% | 5.5% |

The third row of that list is the one that matters most and is easiest to get
wrong. In the original data, only a handful of warehouse-destination lanes carry
an observed freight rate; the rest are imputed at a single shared value. When
most lanes cost the same, routing choice has little leverage, which is why
optimization yields a single-digit percentage saving. A generator that gives
every lane its own distance-based cost creates far more routing headroom than
the real data had and roughly quintuples the apparent benefit.

## Files

| File | Rows | Columns |
|---|---|---|
| `demand.csv` | 7 | `destination`, `demand` |
| `warehouse_capacity.csv` | 19 | `warehouse`, `capacity` |
| `warehouse_cost.csv` | 19 | `warehouse`, `fixed_cost` |
| `transport_cost.csv` | 133 | `warehouse`, `destination`, `cost_per_unit` |

`transport_cost.csv` covers every warehouse-destination pair (19 × 7 = 133).
The model requires complete coverage; `data_processing.py` raises an error if
any lane is missing.

## Regenerating

```bash
python generate_synthetic_data.py
```

Output is deterministic — seed 570, fixed capacity and demand vectors. Re-running
overwrites the four CSVs with byte-identical files.

The CSVs are committed so the model can be run without executing the generator
first.
